records.title: 10R60/10R80 MHT Harsh or Delayed Engagement and Shifts (TSB 22-2428)

records.title: Aviator Transmission Safety Recalls: Park and Direction-Control Defects
records.description: Three separate VIN-scoped transmission recalls affect limited Aviator populations. NHTSA 23V070/Ford 23S06 covers certain 2023 Aviators whose transmission may contain a loose extra bolt that can block the park pawl even when the selector shows Park. NHTSA 25V164/Ford 25S19 covers specified 2025 Aviators built December 4-20, 2024, whose main-control valve body may cause no reverse or unexpected forward motion in Reverse or Neutral. For 26V402, follow the current do-not-drive advisory and contact a Lincoln dealer for transport guidance; the free remedy is updated PCM software plus inspection and replacement of damaged park-system components as needed. For 23S06, the dealer inspects for the loose bolt and replaces the transmission if the inspection fails. For 25S19, the dealer replaces the transmission main-control valve body. Do not buy transmission parts or combine a harsh-shift complaint with these recall remedies without VIN confirmation.

records.title: Unexpected Acceleration and Phantom Braking With Driver-Assist (Co-Pilot360 / BlueCruise) Engaged
records.description: Owners across multiple model years report two opposite but related ADAS misbehaviors. With adaptive cruise / driver-assist (Co-Pilot360, ActiveGlide/BlueCruise) engaged, the Aviator has unexpectedly ACCELERATED toward a stopped vehicle instead of continuing to slow, and separately has applied PHANTOM BRAKING — abrupt, unprompted automatic braking triggered by harmless objects such as a crack in the driveway, overpass shadows, or roadside features. Some events come with 'Antilock brake fault' or 'Pre-Collision Assist not available' messages. These are hard to reproduce on demand and are documented in NHTSA complaints and owner forums; no broad recall specifically targets this behavior.
records.solution: Report any unexpected-acceleration or phantom-braking event to NHTSA (vehicle safety hotline / nhtsa.gov) and to the dealer, with date/time so the module can be scanned for stored events. Ensure all camera/radar sensors are clean, undamaged, and properly aimed (especially after any windshield or bumper work, which requires ADAS recalibration), and that the IPMA/ADAS modules are on the latest software (see related camera/IPMA recalls). Until resolved, use driver-assist features cautiously and keep ready to override with throttle/brake; treat repeated events as a safety concern warranting dealer investigation.

Sudden hard automatic braking for no real obstacle (phantom braking)

records.title: Internal Water Pump Failure Contaminating Engine Oil (3.5L/3.7L V6)
records.description: First-generation MKX models with the 3.5L and 3.7L Duratec/Cyclone V6 use an internal water pump driven off the timing chain inside the engine. When the pump's bearing or seal fails, coolant leaks internally into the oil rather than externally, often with little warning. The result is milky oil on the dipstick/fill cap and, if undetected, coolant-contaminated oil that destroys bearings and scores cylinder walls, leading to engine failure. Repair is labor-intensive (20-30 hours) because the timing cover must be removed, and timing chain/guides are typically serviced at the same time.

records.title: Panoramic Vista Roof Spontaneous Shattering
records.description: Lincoln MKX models with the panoramic Vista Roof have repeated owner reports of the glass spontaneously shattering, sometimes with a loud bang likened to a gunshot, both while parked and while driving at highway speeds. records.title: Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Overheating and Failure on AWD Models
records.description: AWD Lincoln MKX models (first generation, 2007-2015) are prone to power transfer unit failure caused by heat from the nearby exhaust cooking the factory-fill 'lifetime' gear oil, breaking down lubrication. The PTU output shaft seals fail and leak burnt, dark gear oil on the passenger side, often accompanied by a speed-dependent whine, growl, or grinding noise and a burnt-oil smell. Left unaddressed, the unit can seize and damage the transmission. Ford issued TSB 19-2017 for dark fluid leaking from the right-side transfer case intermediate shaft seal.
records.solution: Replace the factory 'lifetime' fluid with full-synthetic 75W-140 gear oil approximately every 30,000 miles as preventive maintenance. If whining, leaking, or a burnt smell is present, replace the PTU seals or the unit before it seizes and damages the transaxle.

records.title: MKZ 3.5L Duratec V6 Internal Water Pump Leak
records.description: The 3.5L Duratec V6 in 2007-2012 MKZ (and shared Edge, Taurus, Flex, Explorer) uses a water pump driven internally by the timing chain. records.title: Electric Power Steering Loss of Assist (Corroded Gear Motor Bolts)
records.description: On 2013-2016 MKZ (and platform-mate Fusion) models, road salt and contaminants can corrode the electric power steering gear motor attachment bolts. records.solution: Under recall 19V632000, dealers replace the steering gear motor bolts and apply a wax sealer free of charge; if bolts are already broken or missing the entire steering gear is replaced. Owners should verify recall status by VIN at nhtsa.gov.

records.title: Harsh / Delayed Automatic Transmission Shifting (6F35)
records.description: MKZ models with the 6F35 6-speed automatic commonly exhibit harsh or delayed engagement, a bump or slip on takeoff, and sluggish acceleration from 0-5 mph. records.title: MKZ EPS Loss of Assist (NHTSA Recall 15V-340 / Ford 15S18)
records.description: Ford issued NHTSA recall 15V-340 (Ford reference 15S18) for 2011-2012 Fusion and MKZ to address sudden loss of electric power steering assist. records.title: 2.0L EcoBoost coolant loss / EGR cooler leak — low coolant, white smoke, overheat
records.description: 2019-2020 Nautilus models with the base 2.0L EcoBoost (non-hybrid) suffer unexplained coolant loss, white tailpipe smoke, an overheat warning, and sometimes coolant intrusion into the cylinders. Ford TSB 20-2234 traces the most common cause to a failing exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) cooler that leaks coolant internally; the related design also has a known coolant-intrusion weakness (narrow coolant slit between cylinders compromising the head-gasket seal). Owners report repeated coolant top-offs with no visible external leak, then misfires as coolant fouls the plugs. A June 2025 Ford EcoBoost coolant-intrusion class action covers 1.5L-2.0L engines; the most severe Nautilus cases require engine replacement with the redesigned block.
records.solution: Per TSB 20-2234, perform a cooling-system pressure test and inspect the EGR cooler; replace the EGR cooler and update PCM software for the typical case. If a coolant smell, white smoke, and cylinder misfires persist (coolant intrusion past the head gasket), the durable fix is a long-block / engine replacement with the updated cross-drilled block — a head-gasket-only repair on the old-style block will fail again. Replace fouled spark plugs and flush the cooling system.

records.title: 2.7L EcoBoost cold-start VCT rattle (top-front-cover tick/tap on startup)
records.description: Nautilus models with the optional 2.7L EcoBoost V6 produce a ticking, tapping, or rattle noise from the top-front-cover area of the engine on initial start-up after a cold soak of 6 hours or more, lasting roughly 2-5 seconds. Using the correct oil viscosity and avoiding extended oil-change intervals helps slow phaser wear. Many out-of-warranty owners report Ford goodwill covering a large portion (one owner quoted ~$2,600 with ~2/3 covered at 88k miles).

records.description: Nautilus models built on or before March 11, 2021 with the 8F35 8-speed automatic commonly exhibit a shudder, buck, hesitation, or jerk while accelerating from a stop up to about 35 mph (57 km/h). records.title: 3.5L EcoBoost Cam Phaser Rattle / Timing Failure
records.description: Fourth-generation Navigators with the twin-turbo 3.5L EcoBoost V6 commonly develop a loud rattle or diesel-like clacking from the front of the engine, most noticeable for 2-5 seconds on cold startup. The internal locking pin inside the variable camshaft timing (VCT) phasers fails, allowing oil to drain and slack to develop in the timing chain. Left unaddressed it can advance to crank/cam correlation faults and timing damage.
records.solution: Ford issued TSB 20-2315 and Customer Satisfaction Program 21N03 (extended warranty to Jan 1, 2023) covering replacement of all four VCT phasers plus a PCM reflash on 2018-2020 models. Out of warranty, repair involves replacing all four phasers, the primary chain, tensioners, and guides.
symptoms: Loud rattle/clatter from front of engine on cold start

records.title: Navigator 3.5L EcoBoost Timing Chain Stretch
records.description: The 3.5L EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 in 2015+ Navigator (and shared F-150, Expedition, Edge ST) suffers timing chain stretch typically between 80,000-150,000 miles. Symptoms include a rattling noise on cold start, particularly on the passenger-side bank, plus P0016/P0017/P0018/P0019 correlation codes. Causes include extended oil change intervals, low-quality oil, and turbocharger-related oil shear.
records.solution: Full timing chain kit replacement (primary chain, both secondary chains, tensioners, guides, sprockets, water pump) — typically $2,500-$4,500 at dealer, $1,800-$3,000 at independent. Stick to 5,000-7,500 mile oil intervals with Motorcraft full-synthetic 5W-30. Catastrophic chain failure means head rebuild ($6,000+).

records.title: 5.4L 3-Valve Triton Spark Plugs Seize and Break in Cylinder Head
records.description: Second- and third-generation Navigators with the 5.4L 3-valve Triton V8 use a unique two-piece spark plug whose long electrode shell extends below the threads. Carbon deposits cake into the gap over high mileage, gripping the plug so tightly that the shell breaks off during removal, leaving a portion seized inside the aluminum cylinder head. This turns a routine tune-up into a costly extraction job.
records.solution: Ford released special extraction tool kits and a procedure: remove plugs only on a cold engine using hand tools, soak with penetrating oil, and break carbon loose gradually. Many owners preemptively replace plugs by ~60k-80k miles to reduce the risk. Broken plugs require an extractor (and sometimes head removal if a fragment falls in).
symptoms: Difficulty removing spark plugs during service
Plug breaks off / shell stuck in head
Misfire if attempted DIY goes wrong
Rough running / check engine light from misfire

records.title: 5.4L 3V Triton Two-Piece Spark Plug Breaks on Removal
records.description: Factory Motorcraft PZT-2FE two-piece platinum plugs in the 5.4L 3V Triton seize in the head from carbon buildup around the ground-electrode shield. Attempting normal removal cracks the plug, leaving the lower shell stuck in the cylinder head and requiring specialized extractor kits or head removal to recover.
records.solution: Soak each plug with penetrating oil (PB Blaster or Seafoam Deep Creep) with engine warm but not hot. Back out 1/8 to 1/4 turn, re-soak, work back and forth before full removal. Use OTC 6918 Triton 3V extractor kit if a plug breaks. Replace with one-piece Champion 7989 or Motorcraft SP-546 (later redesign); apply nickel anti-seize to the smooth lower electrode shell (NOT the threads, per Motorcraft) and torque to 25 ft-lbs.
symptoms: Lower electrode shell stuck in head

records.title: Navigator 5.4L 3V Triton Spark Plug Breakage on Removal
records.description: The 5.4L 3-valve Triton V8 in 2005-2008 Navigator (and shared F-150/Expedition) uses a two-piece spark plug (Motorcraft SP-515/SP-546) that frequently snaps off in the cylinder head during removal. The lower portion stays welded into the head by carbon, leaving the upper electrode in the socket. Common at 60,000-100,000 miles when the first plug change is attempted.
records.solution: Soak each plug 24 hours in penetrating oil (PB Blaster, Seafoam Deep Creep) and remove only when engine is warm. Use the Lisle 65600 / OTC 6918 broken-plug extraction kit if breakage occurs (~$80). Replace with the redesigned one-piece Motorcraft SP-546 / NGK plugs. Ford settled a class-action covering reasonable extraction costs at dealer.

records.title: Air Ride Suspension Compressor Burnout from Air Bag Leaks
records.description: The air suspension's rubber air springs develop pinhole leaks at the upper crimp ring after 8-12 years. 4WD models use a 4-corner system; 2WD models use rear-only. The OEM Continental/AMK compressor (mounted with integrated dryer) runs continuously trying to maintain ride height, eventually burning out. Owners wake to a vehicle sitting on the bump stops and a compressor that hums but no longer builds pressure. NOTE: 4th-generation Navigator (2018+) replaced air suspension with coil-spring adaptive damping and is NOT affected.
records.solution: Diagnose with soapy water at each air spring upper crimp before replacing the compressor. Replace leaking bags in pairs (front or rear) with Arnott/Suncore units and install a new compressor (Arnott P-2932 for 97-06, P-2937/U326 for 07-13) with dryer. For owners who don't tow, Strutmasters/Arnott coil-conversion kits eliminate the problem permanently for $400-700.
symptoms: Vehicle sagging or sitting on rear bump stops in the morning
Compressor runs continuously or won't shut off
Compressor hums but ride height won't rise
Air ride fault message on dash

records.title: Navigator Rear Air Suspension Bag/Compressor Failure
records.description: 2003-2017 Navigators with the optional/standard rear air suspension (and the 2003+ Expedition with the same system) develop air-bag leaks at the bag-to-piston seal as the bag rubber ages and cracks. Symptoms: rear of vehicle sagging overnight, compressor running constantly, error message "Check Air Suspension." Eventually the compressor burns out from constant duty.
records.solution: Replace air bags as a pair (Arnott or Strutmasters aftermarket ~$400-$700 per side; OEM Motorcraft ~$800-$1,200 per side installed). Replace the dryer with the compressor or it will quickly fail again. Some owners convert to coil springs (Strutmasters kit ~$700) — eliminates the leveling feature but is permanent.

records.solution: Recall 25S37 - dealer replaces master cylinder (and booster if contaminated) free of charge. Check VIN at lincoln.com/support/recalls or NHTSA.gov. Do not drive if pedal goes to the floor; have the vehicle towed.

records.title: Deployable Power Running Board Motor Failure & Linkage Corrosion
records.description: The Dorman-supplied power running board motors and pivot/swivel brackets on 2007-2014 (3rd-gen) and 2015-2017 (3rd-gen refresh) Navigators corrode and seize from road salt and water exposure, especially in northern states. Boards stop deploying, hang in mid-position, or cycle repeatedly. Brackets with dissimilar-metal mounting can crack and drop the board. On 2018+ (4th-gen) trucks the failures are more often electrical/settings-related (boards switching from AUTO to OFF, one-side-only operation) rather than pure mechanical corrosion.
records.solution: Pull the affected board, free the linkage with PB Blaster, lube all pivots with marine grease. If motor is dead, OE replacement (Ford 9L7Z-16A507-A family) is ~$500/side, aftermarket Dorman motor+bracket assemblies run $150-300. On 2018+ trucks, first verify board mode is set to AUTO and check battery health before replacing hardware. Scan the BCM for B-codes to confirm which side before ordering.
symptoms: Running board stuck open or closed
Board cycles in/out repeatedly while driving
One side works, the other doesn't

records.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Failure (Clicking, Wrong Temperature)

records.title: SYNC 3 / SYNC 4 Infotainment Freezing, Black Screen, and Touch Unresponsiveness
records.description: The SYNC 3 (2018-2020) and SYNC 4 (2021+) head unit in the 4th-generation Navigator freezes, reboots mid-drive, displays a black screen with spinning loader, loses touch response, drops Bluetooth pairing, or fails to show the backup camera. Issue is typically an APIM (Accessory Protocol Interface Module) firmware bug or hardware fault. Note: The 2015 Navigator (final year of 3rd-gen) is the only Navigator that ever shipped with MyLincoln Touch / SYNC 2; 2010-2014 Navigators ran SYNC 1, a different system not affected by the MyFord/MyLincoln Touch class action.
records.solution: Soft reset: hold power + seek-right ~10 seconds until reboot. If that fails, perform a master reset (Settings > General > Master Reset) and install the latest SYNC update from owner.lincoln.com via USB. For persistent failure, disconnect the negative battery cable for 10 minutes. Dealer APIM replacement runs $800-1500 if the module is dead. The MyFord/MyLincoln Touch class settlement (Case 3:13-cv-03072) only covered Ford/Lincoln vehicles purchased before August 9, 2013, and the claim period has closed — Navigator owners are not eligible since the Navigator did not receive MyLincoln Touch until MY2015.

records.title: Town Car Rear Air Suspension Bag/Compressor Failure
records.description: Final-gen Town Car (2003-2011 Panther platform) used a rear-only air suspension that develops bag leaks and compressor burnout very similar to the Navigator/Crown Vic Police Interceptor system. Cars sag dramatically overnight; compressor cycles continually trying to refill.
records.solution: Replace bags as a pair ($300-$600 aftermarket installed). Compressor + dryer kit ~$200-$400 installed. Many owners convert to coil springs with a Strutmasters-style kit (~$300-$500) — loses self-leveling but no further maintenance. Limo owners need to keep air for headroom adjustment.

records.title: Town Car HVAC Blend Door Actuator Clicking / No-Heat
records.description: Town Car (and shared Crown Vic / Grand Marquis) HVAC blend door actuators fail commonly, presenting as a persistent rapid clicking from behind the dash followed by no temperature control — usually stuck blowing cold on the driver side or hot on the passenger side. Plastic gear teeth strip; replacement is the only fix.
records.solution: Replacement blend door actuator ($30-$80 part) — labor varies wildly by which actuator. Driver side: 30 min. Passenger side: 1-2 hours. Floor/defrost actuator (deepest): 3-5 hours. Aftermarket Dorman actuators have mixed reviews — Motorcraft OEM lasts longer.
symptoms: one side cold one side hot

records.title: Coil-on-Plug Ignition Coil Failure and Misfires (4.6L V8)
records.description: The 1998-up 4.6L 2V V8 uses eight individual coil-on-plug ignition coils whose boots and towers crack with age and heat, allowing spark to track to ground and causing single- or multi-cylinder misfires, rough idle, and stumbling under load. Failures are accelerated when the 1996-2001 plastic intake manifold leaks coolant into the spark plug wells and shorts the coils. It is one of the most common drivability complaints on the platform, well documented across owner forums and diagnostic guides.
records.solution: Diagnose by swapping the suspect coil to another cylinder and confirming the misfire code follows; replace failed coils and boots, and replace high-mileage spark plugs at the same time. If coolant is found in a plug well, fix the intake manifold leak first or the new coil will fail too.
symptoms: Check engine light, sometimes flashing, with misfire codes
Stumble or jerking under acceleration or load

records.title: Fuel Tank Puncture and Fire Risk in Rear Impacts (Livery/Limousine Shield Program)
records.description: The Panther platform mounts the fuel tank behind the rear axle, and on 1992-2001 cars a small tab on the rear stabilizer-bar axle bracket (and the left shock-mount bracket) can puncture the tank in a high-energy rear collision, causing post-crash fuel leaks and fires that have killed occupants in otherwise survivable crashes. NHTSA closed its investigation in 2002 without a recall, but Ford issued a 2001 TSB to grind the tab flush, began installing protective shield kits on police Crown Victorias in 2002, and — after a fatal 2003 limousine fire — extended free shield kits to Town Car limousine/livery operators in September 2005. Documented by the Center for Auto Safety and multiple wrongful-death lawsuits.
records.solution: Have the Ford TSB performed (grind the stabilizer-bar bracket tab flush) and install the Ford rear-axle fuel tank shield kit, which was offered free to Town Car limousine/livery operators and costs roughly $100 in parts for civilian cars. Verify with a dealer whether the shield was ever installed.
symptoms: No fuel tank shield kit present over the axle brackets (visible during inspection)
Sharp un-ground tab on the rear stabilizer-bar axle bracket facing the tank
Fuel odor or leak after even a moderate rear-end impact
Applies especially to limousine, livery, and fleet cars with added rear weight

records.title: Lighting Control Module (LCM) Failure — Headlights Cut Out
records.description: The Town Car's Lighting Control Module — the relay-filled black box that runs the headlamps, parking, marker, tail, and autolamp functions — fails as internal relay contacts wear and solder joints crack, causing flickering or total loss of headlights, lights stuck on (draining the battery), or high beams locked on. The identical-design LCM in the sister Panther cars (2003-2005 Crown Victoria and Grand Marquis) was the subject of NHTSA safety recall 15V-861 (Ford 15S39, ~296,000 vehicles) for cracked solder joints causing loss of headlights, but the Town Car was never included in that recall despite the same well-documented failure pattern in NHTSA complaints and owner forums. Losing headlights while driving at night is a genuine crash risk.
records.solution: Replace the LCM or send it to a board-level rebuild service (around $150-250) that replaces the failure-prone relays and re-flows the solder joints; rebuilds keep the module's VIN programming. On 2003-2005 cars, the bypass-module kit Ford developed for recall 15S39 on Crown Victoria/Grand Marquis addresses the same headlamp relay circuit.

records.title: Plastic Intake Manifold Coolant Crossover Failure (Class-Action Defect)
records.description: From 1996 to mid-2001, the 4.6L V8 used an all-composite (Nylon 6/6) intake manifold whose front coolant crossover cracks with heat-cycling age, leaking coolant — often from the hidden underside — or failing outright and dumping the cooling system over the engine. The defect affected up to 2 million Panther-platform cars and was the subject of a Ford class-action settlement (announced December 2005) that reimbursed owners at least $735 for manifold repairs on 1996-2001 Town Cars, Crown Victorias, and Grand Marquis. Left unrepaired, the leak causes overheating and can cook the engine; coolant also pools in spark plug wells and destroys ignition coils.
records.solution: Replace the manifold with the revised design (DuPont Zytel composite with an aluminum front coolant crossover, used from mid-2001/2002 onward; Dorman and Ford service parts both use the aluminum crossover). Replace any coolant-soaked coils and pressure-test the system afterward.

Coolant level dropping with frequent top-offs
Visible coolant seep or steam at the front crossover near the alternator
Sudden large coolant dump and overheating
Coolant standing in the spark plug wells

records.title: Power Steering Rack and Line Leaks (2003+ Rack-and-Pinion)
records.description: The 2003 Panther-platform redesign replaced the recirculating-ball steering box with rack-and-pinion steering, and as these cars age the rack's pinion and end seals plus the high-pressure line fittings and O-rings are frequent leak points. Leaks at the pressure-line fitting and pressure switch are also commonly reported on the earlier cars, but rack seal leakage is the characteristic late-car failure.
records.solution: Replace the leaking component: a damaged O-ring or high-pressure line is a cheap fix, while a leaking rack is normally replaced with a remanufactured unit followed by a front toe alignment. Flush old fluid and verify the pump was not run dry.

records.title: Steering Intermediate Shaft Corrosion — Loss of Steering (Recall 13V-385)
records.description: On 2005-2011 Town Cars (and sister Crown Victoria/Grand Marquis) operated in road-salt states, severe corrosion can seize the lower intermediate steering shaft, which can cause the upper intermediate shaft to collapse and the steering column lower bearing to separate — resulting in loss of steering control. records.solution: Have a Ford/Lincoln dealer perform recall 13V-385 free of charge: replace the lower intermediate shaft, inspect and repair the upper shaft and column lower bearing, and install a retainer clip if the bearing has separated. Check the VIN for open recall status; out-of-scope cars need the shafts replaced at a shop.
symptoms: Notchy or binding feel when turning the wheel
Clunking or popping from the steering column
Visible heavy rust on the intermediate steering shaft
